1.title: SDKs, Serialization and Streaming Data
1.text: Welcome to Module three: S D Ks, Serialization and Streaming Data. It covers the exam area Domain one: Development with A W S Services. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do four things. Develop code that interacts with A W S services by using A P Is and S D Ks (one point one.five). Manage streaming data by using A W S services (one point one.six). Serialize and deserialize data to integrate application code with A W S services (one point one.seven). Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Exam area: Domain one: Development with A W S Services (thirty percent). Exam format: fifty scored questions, multiple choice and multiple response; a score of seven hundred twenty on a scale of one hundred to one thousand passes. Validated against: the official A W S Developer Associate (D V A-C three) exam guide.

1.title: APIs, the CLI and the SDKs
1.text: A P Is, the C L I and the S D Ks. Every A W S service is an H T T P S A P I. You reach it through the A W S S D Ks (Python, Java Script, Java and more), the A W S C L I, or Cloud Shell. Requests are signed with Signature Version four; the S D K does this for you.

1.title: APIs, the CLI and the SDKs, continued
1.text: A P Is, the C L I and the S D Ks. Credentials. The S D K looks through a credential provider chain: environment variables, shared credentials and config files, then role credentials from the container, instance or Lambda execution role. Region. Set the Region in code, config or environment; most calls fail or hit the wrong place without it. Retries. S D Ks retry throttling and transient errors with backoff; you can set the retry mode and maximum attempts.

1.title: APIs, the CLI and the SDKs, continued
1.text: A P Is, the C L I and the S D Ks. Pagination. List calls return pages; follow the next token (or use the S D K paginator). Waiters. Poll until a resource reaches a state (for example, an instance is running). Timeouts. Set connect and read timeouts for resilient code.

1.title: APIs, the CLI and the SDKs, continued
1.text: A P Is, the C L I and the S D Ks. The figure shows this: The S D K credential provider chain and the call to a service endpoint. Exam tip: Code running on A W S should use a role, not access keys in code. The S D K picks the role up from the credential chain automatically.

1.title: Serialization and deserialization
1.text: Serialization and deserialization. Serialization turns an in-memory object into bytes or text to send or store; deserialization reverses it. Jason. A P I Gateway, Lambda events, S Q S and S N S message bodies. Base sixty-four. Binary data inside Jason (A P I Gateway binary payloads, some Lambda event bodies). Dynamo D B attribute values. The low-level A P I uses typed values such as S text and N forty-two; document or resource clients marshal native types for you. Avro, Protobuf, Parquet. Streaming and analytics formats. Always validate and handle bad input when you deserialize, and watch character encoding (U T F-eight).

1.title: Streaming data
1.text: Streaming data. The figure shows this: Producers, a Kinesis data stream with shards, and consumers.

1.title: Streaming data, continued
1.text: Streaming data. Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Real-time stream you read yourself; shards give capacity; a partition key decides the shard. Amazon Data Firehose. Loads streams into S three, Open Search and other destinations with buffering; optional Lambda transformation; no shards to manage. Dynamo D B Streams. Change records of table writes, read by Lambda.

1.title: Kinesis Data Streams essentials
1.text: Kinesis Data Streams essentials. Shard capacity. About one megabyte or s or one thousand records or s in, two megabytes or s out per shard. Partition key. Same key goes to the same shard, preserving order per key; a hot key overloads one shard. Too fast. Provisioned Throughput Exceeded Exception means add shards, spread keys, or retry with backoff. Consumers. Lambda event source mapping, the Kinesis Client Library, or enhanced fan-out for dedicated throughput per consumer. Retention. twenty-four hours by default, extendable (up to three sixty-five days). Exam tip: Need custom real-time processing and replay equals Kinesis Data Streams. Need to land data in S three with minimal code equals Firehose. Exam tip: A hot Kinesis partition key overloads one shard. Spread keys or add shards, and retry with backoff on Provisioned Throughput Exceeded Exception.

1.title: Practice Question 1
1.text: Question one. An application running on E C two must call Dynamo D B. What is the best way to provide credentials? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Attach an I A M role to the instance and let the S D K find it. The S D K credential chain uses role credentials from the instance automatically.

1.title: Practice Question 2
1.text: Question two. A list call returns only the first one hundred items. What should the code do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Follow the next token or use a paginator. List A P Is return pages; follow the next token.

1.title: Practice Question 3
1.text: Question three. Producers write many records with the same partition key and one shard is overloaded. What is the likely cause? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A hot partition key. The same key always maps to the same shard.

1.title: Practice Question 4
1.text: Question four. A team wants to deliver streaming clickstream data to S three with minimal code and no shard management. Which service fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Amazon Data Firehose. Firehose loads streams into destinations with buffering and no shards to manage.

1.title: Practice Question 5
1.text: Question five. Binary image data must travel inside a Jason body. What is the usual encoding? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Base sixty-four. Base sixty-four encodes binary data as text for Jason.

1.title: Practice Question 6
1.text: Question six. A consumer needs dedicated read throughput that does not compete with other consumers of the same stream. What should be used? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Enhanced fan-out. Enhanced fan-out gives each consumer its own throughput.

1.title: Recall Check 1
1.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What signs A W S A P I requests? Answer: Signature Version four, applied by the S D K. Question two. Where does the S D K find role credentials? Answer: In the credential provider chain (container, instance or Lambda role). Question three. What decides which Kinesis shard gets a record? Answer: The partition key.

1.title: Recall Check 2
1.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the default Kinesis retention? Answer: twenty-four hours. Question five. What does Firehose do? Answer: Buffers and delivers streaming data to destinations such as S three and Open Search. Question six. What is serialization? Answer: Turning an in-memory object into bytes or text to send or store.

1.title: Module Recap
1.text: Here is the recap. S D K: credential chain (use roles), Region, retries, pagination, waiters. Serialization: Jason, base sixty-four, Dynamo D B typed values. Kinesis Data Streams: shards, partition key, twenty-four h retention, enhanced fan-out. Firehose: managed delivery to S three and others, buffering, no shards.
